sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq (1320-25)**: Established the dynasty after defeating Khusrau Khan; focused on **restoration of order** and irrigation works.
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325-51)**: Known for **radical experiments** (Token Currency, Capital Shift, Khurasan Expedition) aimed at centralizing power and expanding the tax base.
• **Firoz Shah Tughlaq (1351-88)**: Shifted to **appeasement policies** (Ulema, nobility, army) and massive public works; introduced the **hereditary Iqta system**.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The transition from a centralized military state under Muhammad bin Tughlaq to a decentralized, welfare-oriented, but militarily weak state under Firoz Shah.

Firoz Shah Tughlaq allowed soldiers to pass their land grants to their sons, leading to the decline of central control over the military.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Public Works (FST)**: Construction of 300 towns (Hissar, Firozabad, Jaunpur) and extensive canal networks.
• **Welfare State**: Establishment of 'Dar-ul-Shifa' (hospitals) and 'Diwan-i-Khairat' (charity department).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Rebellion of provincial governors (Bahmani/Vijayanagara emergence); economic exhaustion from failed experiments.
• **Solutions**: FST's focus on administrative consolidation and religious orthodoxy to stabilize the throne.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'G-M-F' (Ghiyas, Muhammad, Firoz).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Ghiyas (Founder/Order), Muhammad (Experiments/Expansion), Firoz (Welfare/Decentralization).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Token Currency' failure with 'Debasement of currency'. MBT's currency was a state-backed token, not a debasement of metal content.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Administrative Overreach' to describe Muhammad bin Tughlaq's policies and 'Patrimonial Bureaucracy' for Firoz Shah's reforms.

keyTakeaways: The Tughlaq period marks the transition from the Sultanate's peak to its fragmentation.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq's policies were theoretically sound but practically flawed due to poor implementation.
Firoz Shah Tughlaq's reforms provided short-term stability but weakened the long-term structural integrity of the Sultanate.
